questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial for me to go on exchange in an English speaking country both because I am use to studying in English but also because a part of the reason why I choose to go on exchange was to become better in English. I choose to apply for study in Australia because I have heard from friends and family that they have some of the best universities and saw it as an opportunities to study at prestige university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I have had a great experience with by exchange but academic but also social and learning about a new culture.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, University of Sydney have been really good at giving information both before and during the semester.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We have a contact person here in Sydney and she could help with almost everything, I had problems with my login to the USYD portal and they helped me very quickly.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: No not very easy but when we did find our apartment it was okay, the only reason why we choose off campus housing was because the on campus housing is way to expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Use Facebook marketplace to search for apartment, very good and very effective.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I recieved an email explaining step by step how to register at my institution and it was super easy to follow and no problems, even when I had a problem with creating my password and getting access they solved it very quickly.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Both my contact person at USYD but also the hole administration.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful, I got all the units I wanted and there was no problems when applying for them.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Follow the guidelines and you won't have any problems

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took only undergrad units at USYD, because as a BA student they were the only ones available.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different mostly because of how they grade you in percentage and we have had both participation grades and a lot more assignments during the semester, and these assignments also counts in our final grade which is very different from UCPH

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Digital Business Innovation, Introduction To Interface Design, Leadership, and Responsible Design for Innovation.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Introduction to interface design and leadership.

questions.answer: Din't go to any non-academic activities

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Just enjoy Sydney and the places around there is a lot to see.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go out in the weekends

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There isn't so many cultural differences

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people are so open and kind and very sweet to everybody which has been very nice and easy to be here.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't live on campus, apply for at student OPAL card and follow Bondi_lines on Instagram

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Which kind of OPAL card to use

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the people I have met

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding a place to live which was within my budget
